spider-1-0.description: Write a query for a database not seen in training, given a question and its schema.
spider-1-0.input: A question and a relational schema
spider-1-0.assessment: Report the evaluator: original exact-set match or later test-suite execution accuracy.
spider-1-0.date_note: First arXiv submission for the original Spider benchmark.

codexglue.description: Compare models across code search, translation, completion and other programming-language tasks.
codexglue.input: Code, text queries or paired snippets, by subtask
codexglue.assessment: Task-specific metrics including accuracy, F1 and BLEU
codexglue.date_note: Microsoft tool listing, followed the next day by its public announcement.

apps.description: Write Python programs that meet a problem specification; passing some tests differs from solving the problem.
apps.input: Programming problem and required input/output behavior
apps.assessment: Fraction of tests passed and all-tests accuracy

humaneval.description: Complete a Python function from its signature and docstring, then run unit tests.
humaneval.input: Python function signature, docstring and examples

mbpp.description: Translate a short English programming task into a Python function that satisfies its tests.
mbpp.input: Short Python task description and test assertions
mbpp.output: Python program implementing the requested behavior
mbpp.assessment: Generated code run against unit tests

codecontests.description: Write complete programs for competition problems and check them against input/output test cases.
codecontests.assessment: Program output checked on test cases
codecontests.date_note: Original AlphaCode announcement naming the competition dataset.

evalplus.description: Evaluate generated programs more rigorously by extending the tests for an existing synthesis benchmark.
evalplus.input: Python synthesis prompts from the underlying benchmark
evalplus.assessment: Pass@k under expanded functional test suites

bird.description: Translate a question into SQL over large, real databases where correctness and query efficiency both matter.
bird.input: Database, schema, question and external knowledge
bird.assessment: Execution accuracy and efficiency of correct queries

swe-bench.description: Modify a real Python repository to resolve a GitHub issue; regression tests judge the patch.
swe-bench.input: Repository snapshot and corresponding GitHub issue
swe-bench.assessment: Required issue-fixing and regression tests must pass
swe-bench.date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.
swe-bench.first_author_affil: Princeton University and Princeton Language and Intelligence

livecodebench.description: The cumulative code-generation snapshot contains 400 problems from May 2023 through Mar 2024. A narrower contest-date filter selects a different evaluation.
livecodebench.input: A contest problem statement and examples
livecodebench.assessment: Pass@1 or reported pass@k on the specified snapshot and problem-date window.
livecodebench.date_note: Original public paper and substantive data upload share March 12 UTC.

alternative_dates.note: Publisher dataset commit identifying the edition.

scicode.description: Implement a scientific computation from a problem description, often by composing smaller scientific subproblems.
scicode.input: A scientific problem and its component specifications
scicode.assessment: Scientist-authored test cases assess subproblems and full solutions
scicode.date_note: Original paper v1; distinguish runs with and without the optional scientific background.
scicode.first_author_affil: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Argonne National Laboratory

swe-bench-verified.description: Run the SWE-bench repair task on a human-validated subset of 500 issues.
swe-bench-verified.input: Human-validated issue and matching repository snapshot
swe-bench-verified.assessment: Same test-based resolution criterion, on 500 validated issues
swe-bench-verified.date_note: Existing entry and stable slug; bare family labels need source context before assigning an edition result.

spider-2-0-lite.description: Write SQL from supplied database metadata and documentation. Lite is the text-to-SQL track, not the full Spider 2.0 agent workflow.
spider-2-0-lite.input: A question, database metadata and reference documentation
spider-2-0-lite.output: SQL for the target database dialect
spider-2-0-lite.assessment: Compare query results with the reference under the Lite execution evaluator.
spider-2-0-lite.date_note: The first Spider 2.0 preprint describes Lite separately from the full workflow benchmark.

code-arena-webdev.description: Two models build web apps from the same request. A voter tries both apps before picking a favorite or declaring a tie.
code-arena-webdev.input: The same user-supplied web development brief for two models
code-arena-webdev.output: Two runnable web apps for side-by-side comparison
code-arena-webdev.assessment: Pairwise user votes are aggregated into Bradley–Terry ratings; there is no fixed pass mark.
code-arena-webdev.date_note: Original WebDev Arena launch, linked by Arena’s March 2025 retrospective; this entry covers the WebDev track, not all of Code Arena or Text Arena (Coding).

terminal-bench.description: Complete multi-step tasks in a terminal; task-specific tests inspect the final environment.
terminal-bench.input: Terminal task instruction and a prepared container
terminal-bench.output: Shell actions and resulting files or system state
terminal-bench.date_note: The May announcement calls the original suite Core-v0; the 2.0 announcement calls the May release 1.0. These are not separate launch dates.

deepswe.description: Implement an original engineering task in an existing repository. The tests check the requested behavior rather than matching a reference patch.
deepswe.input: A repository at a fixed revision and an engineering brief
deepswe.assessment: Pass rate under task-specific behavioral tests for the originally released tasks and grading protocol.

gamecraft-bench.description: Build a playable Godot game from a design brief. The agent submits the project and demonstrates its behavior with replayable inputs.
gamecraft-bench.input: A game specification, Godot workspace and shared assets
gamecraft-bench.output: A complete game project and replayable input traces
gamecraft-bench.assessment: A judge scores the replay for game mechanics, content depth, visual feedback and presentation.
gamecraft-bench.date_note: First arXiv submission (v1, UTC). Scores the generated game as demonstrated in replay, not the model’s ability to play existing games.
gamecraft-bench.first_author_affil: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Shenzhen Loop Area Institute

cwe-bench-v2.description: Assess security fixes to real repositories while checking that previously working behavior still holds.
cwe-bench-v2.output: Code changes resolving the identified weakness

terminal-bench-2-0.description: Complete harder terminal tasks with independently checked final outcomes. The 2.0 release introduced a new task suite and Harbor.
terminal-bench-2-0.input: A task brief and a configured terminal environment
terminal-bench-2-0.output: Files, program outputs or a changed environment
terminal-bench-2-0.assessment: Share of tasks completed under their task-specific verifiers.
terminal-bench-2-0.date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

terminal-bench-2-1.description: Run the revised 2.0 suite. The authors corrected 28 of its 89 tasks, so matching the model alone does not make scores comparable.
terminal-bench-2-1.input: An 89-task terminal suite with corrected task definitions
terminal-bench-2-1.assessment: Task completion under the corrected instructions and verifiers.
terminal-bench-2-1.date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

terminal-bench-3-0.description: Complete 74 challenging terminal workflows drawn from seven domains in the first 3.0 task set.
terminal-bench-3-0.input: A work request and a configured terminal environment
terminal-bench-3-0.output: A verified artifact or state change
terminal-bench-3-0.assessment: Pass rate under the 3.0 task verifiers.
terminal-bench-3-0.date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dates.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

terminal-bench-4-0.description: The 4.0 release removes eight 3.0 tasks, fixes others and recalibrates compute and time limits.
terminal-bench-4-0.input: The 66-task terminal suite and its 4.0 resource settings
terminal-bench-4-0.assessment: Share of tasks passing the 4.0 checks under the specified resources.
terminal-bench-4-0.date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dates.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

terminal-bench-4-1.description: The agent-facing 4.0 tasks remain the same; revised verifiers regrade the resulting artifacts.
terminal-bench-4-1.input: The same 66 agent-facing terminal tasks as 4.0
terminal-bench-4-1.assessment: Share passing the revised 4.1 verifiers; saved 4.0 outputs can be regraded.
terminal-bench-4-1.date_note: Project release announcement, as dated in its official news index.

alternative_dates.note: GitHub release published_at (UTC); the project announcement has its own later date.

harnesseval.description: Compare review frameworks on real pull requests with reference findings. This is dsifry’s scored evaluation, not a new PR dataset or the MirroS workflow.
harnesseval.input: A pull request and review instructions
harnesseval.output: Review findings about the proposed change
harnesseval.assessment: Check findings against the reference evaluation and report precision, recall and cost for the specified run.
harnesseval.date_note: The public report is documented by this commit; this is not its first-ever release date.

harness-exam.description: Give a coding agent a small set of practical tasks, including rewriting web content and reasoning over a novel. The project checks submitted answers.
harness-exam.input: Task instructions and supplied source material
harness-exam.output: An answer for each exam task
harness-exam.assessment: The scorecard counts tasks passed out of the total, not a human preference vote.
harness-exam.date_note: The scorecard existed in this dated repository commit.

frontiercode.description: Solve engineering tasks authored by maintainers of real open-source repositories. Main, Extended and Diamond refer to nested subsets.
frontiercode.input: A repository and a maintainer-defined engineering brief
frontiercode.assessment: Maintainer-defined rubrics, with blocking criteria and a weighted score.

frontiercode-1-1.description: Resolve repository tasks with revised scoring criteria; the publisher reports Main and Extended and drops the Diamond subset.
frontiercode-1-1.input: A repository and a maintainer-defined engineering brief
frontiercode-1-1.assessment: Revised weighted rubrics and blocking criteria, on the specified subset.

frontiercode-2-0.description: Address a new set of engineering tasks drawn from a broader range of repositories and request categories.
frontiercode-2-0.input: A repository and a maintainer-defined engineering brief
frontiercode-2-0.assessment: Repository-specific checks assess whether the change is mergeable under the 2.0 protocol.

cursorbench.description: Solve the coding tasks in Cursor’s initial public changelog edition, emphasizing code edits, refactors and bug fixes.
cursorbench.input: Coding brief, repository context and tools
cursorbench.output: A code change or other task-specific response
cursorbench.assessment: Score under that CursorBench task set and run budget; latency and cost are reported separately.
cursorbench.date_note: Cursor’s public leaderboard changelog explicitly labels this as a Tasks entry, not a reporting-only pricing change.

cursorbench-3-1.description: The task suite adds codebase understanding, planning and code review; grading was also revised for some edit tasks.
cursorbench-3-1.input: Coding brief, repository context and tools
cursorbench-3-1.output: A code change or other task-specific response
cursorbench-3-1.assessment: Score under that CursorBench task set and run budget; latency and cost are reported separately.
cursorbench-3-1.date_note: Cursor’s public leaderboard changelog explicitly labels this as a Tasks entry, not a reporting-only pricing change.

cursorbench-3-2.description: The suite adds instruction-following and advanced tool-use problems.
cursorbench-3-2.input: Coding brief, repository context and tools
cursorbench-3-2.output: A code change or other task-specific response
cursorbench-3-2.assessment: Score under that CursorBench task set and run budget; latency and cost are reported separately.
cursorbench-3-2.date_note: Cursor’s public leaderboard changelog explicitly labels this as a Tasks entry, not a reporting-only pricing change.

cursorbench-4-0.description: The suite introduces longer-horizon tasks covering code edits, investigation, intent understanding and design adherence.
cursorbench-4-0.input: Coding brief, repository context and tools
cursorbench-4-0.output: A code change or other task-specific response
cursorbench-4-0.assessment: Score under that CursorBench task set and run budget; latency and cost are reported separately.
cursorbench-4-0.date_note: Cursor’s public leaderboard changelog explicitly labels this as a Tasks entry, not a reporting-only pricing change.

cursorbench-4-1.description: The release changes instruction-following problems and increases the agent time limit.
cursorbench-4-1.input: Coding brief, repository context and tools
cursorbench-4-1.output: A code change or other task-specific response
cursorbench-4-1.assessment: Score under that CursorBench task set and run budget; latency and cost are reported separately.
cursorbench-4-1.date_note: Cursor’s public leaderboard changelog explicitly labels this as a Tasks entry, not a reporting-only pricing change.

deepswe-1-1.description: Complete the original engineering tasks under a revised execution and grading protocol.
deepswe-1-1.input: A repository snapshot and an engineering task
deepswe-1-1.assessment: Tests grade the submitted patch in a clean environment, not the agent’s transient workspace.

cwe-bench-v0.description: The original defensive assessment evaluates repository fixes across categories of software weakness.
cwe-bench-v0.input: A repository and a defensive repair requirement
cwe-bench-v0.assessment: Programmatic checks assess the requested repair and previously supported behavior.

cwe-bench-v1.description: A revised defensive assessment of repository fixes, with expanded task coverage and updated programmatic checks.
cwe-bench-v1.input: A repository and a defensive repair requirement
cwe-bench-v1.assessment: Programmatic checks assess the requested repair and previously supported behavior.

swe-bench-lite.description: A 300-task test subset selected for cost-effective evaluation on self-contained repository issues.
swe-bench-lite.input: An issue description and its repository snapshot
swe-bench-lite.assessment: Fraction of selected issues resolved by the test harness.
swe-bench-lite.date_note: The project dates Lite to March 2024; this is the author’s dated full dataset upload, not an empty repository creation event.

swe-bench-multimodal.description: The initial multimodal software engineering release uses 517 issues with visual evidence from JavaScript projects.
swe-bench-multimodal.input: A repository, issue description and associated visual evidence
swe-bench-multimodal.assessment: Fraction of issues resolved on the original evaluation split.
swe-bench-multimodal.date_note: Original paper v1. An unversioned result reported after September 1, 2026 does not by itself establish use of the v2 test split.

swe-bench-multimodal-v2.description: The V2 edition keeps 480 reproducible issues, drops flaky or ungradeable tests, and publishes its full test split and tooling.
swe-bench-multimodal-v2.input: A repository, issue description and associated visual evidence
swe-bench-multimodal-v2.assessment: Fraction of the V2 issues resolved, using the revised visual-asset and JavaScript evaluation pipeline.

swe-bench-multilingual.description: Evaluate repository patches on 300 tasks drawn from 42 repositories in nine programming languages. It is not Multi-SWE-bench.
swe-bench-multilingual.input: An issue description and project files in the task’s programming language
swe-bench-multilingual.assessment: Fraction of instances passing the task’s repository tests.
swe-bench-multilingual.date_note: First substantive maintainer dataset upload located. “Multilingual” refers to programming languages, not translations of the same prompts.

swe-bench-pro.description: Scale’s independently produced suite tests long-horizon engineering work. Public, held-out and commercial splits are not interchangeable.
swe-bench-pro.input: A repository snapshot and engineering requirement
swe-bench-pro.assessment: Task resolution under the specified split and repository test harness.
swe-bench-pro.date_note: Scale’s Pro suite is distinct from the original Princeton-led dataset. Preserve public/held-out qualifiers; unsuffixed later reports need version evidence.

swe-bench-pro-v2.description: Scale refreshes the public Pro split and its execution protocol, including validated checks and network-restricted evaluation.
swe-bench-pro-v2.input: A repository snapshot and Pro V2 task specification
swe-bench-pro-v2.assessment: Task resolution on the V2 public split under its published run protocol.

livecodebench-v2.description: The cumulative code-generation snapshot contains 511 problems from May 2023 through May 2024. A narrower contest-date filter selects a different evaluation.
livecodebench-v2.input: A contest problem statement and examples
livecodebench-v2.assessment: Pass@1 or reported pass@k on the specified snapshot and problem-date window.
livecodebench-v2.date_note: This date is the publisher’s versioned dataset commit, not the last contest date in the problem window.

alternative_dates.note: Publisher dataset commit identifying the edition.

livecodebench-v4.date_note: This date is the publisher’s versioned dataset commit, not the last contest date in the problem window.

livecodebench-v5.input: A contest problem statement and examples
livecodebench-v5.assessment: Pass@1 or reported pass@k on the specified snapshot and problem-date window.

livecodebench-v6.input: A contest problem statement and examples
livecodebench-v6.assessment: Pass@1 or reported pass@k on the specified snapshot and problem-date window.
livecodebench-v6.date_note: This date is the publisher’s versioned dataset commit, not the last contest date in the problem window.

swe-arena.description: Compare models on iterative software requests.
swe-arena.input: A user request and the evolving code or conversation.
swe-arena.output: Candidate solutions to the same software task.
swe-arena.assessment: Interactive comparisons; evaluation depends on the selected task and comparison mode.
